work_item.title: Create artifacts/project-summary.md
work_item.description: Create a concise project summary document for Engineering Loop v11.3 at `artifacts/project-summary.md`.
acceptance_criteria: Covers all six required sections: purpose, architecture, key components, core principles, and directory structure
Key components section includes subsections for: stages, skills, references, and orchestrator
Uses markdown formatting with headers, tables, and code blocks where appropriate
Accurately reflects v11.3 features including dynamic graph, dual-mode architecture, and surgical CLI

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.content: Brief description of Engineering Loop as a persistent while-loop engine for AI-assisted software development, orchestrating specialized AI sub-agents through the complete SDLC using a dynamic graph that adapts to work item complexity, type, and context. Mention local model support.

sections.heading: Architecture
sections.content: Multi-project via git submodule (.eng/ read-only, project artifacts gitignored). Dual-mode execution (Python CLI deterministic LangGraph vs LLM Prompt mode following generated topology). Dynamic graph construction via GraphBuilder. Two-layer config (template + project override).

subsections.name: Stages
subsections.content: 26 stages across 7 phases (Init, Design, Architecture, Implementation, Verify/QA, Deploy, Doc/Post). Table mapping phases to stage IDs. Each stage follows Design→Execute→Validate pattern with Essence gate.

subsections.name: Skills
subsections.content: 11 built-in skills (bmad-integration, verifier, solution-designer, etc.) + 7 self-constructed at runtime from templates. List key skills.

subsections.name: References
subsections.content: 15 shared reference documents loaded by ID on demand (essence-sidecar, bmad-ideation-patterns, exit-conditions, etc.).

subsections.name: Orchestrator
subsections.content: eng_loop/ Python package on LangGraph. Key modules: graph_builder.py, node_registry.py, edge_rules.py, schemas.py, cli.py, state.py, routing.py, model.py. CLI commands: --dynamic-graph, --build-topology, --check-compliance, surgical ops.

sections.heading: Core Principles
sections.content: Numbered list of 17 principles: dynamic graph construction, programmatic flow control, structured output (Pydantic), evidence gates, declarative routing, progressive disclosure, context slicing, context optimization (ProjectMap + tool cache), full loop enforcement, Essence before every stage, auto-sizing, TDD per task, independent verification, parallel QA, continuous decisions (AD-NNN), self-improving lessons, surgical CLI operations.

sections.heading: Directory Structure
sections.content: Tree diagram showing: stages/ (24 procedure files), skills/ (11 built-in), references/ (15 docs), eng_loop/src/eng_loop/ (orchestrator), setup/ (install scripts), artifacts/ (runtime: architectures/, blueprints/, bdd-journeys/, design/, test-plans/, graph-topology.*), plus root files (config-template.yaml, state-template.json, skill-index.md, ORCHESTRATOR.md, CORE.md, README.md, START.md, AGENTS.md).

data_sources.README.md: Primary source for overview, principles, stages table, directory structure
data_sources.CORE.md: Stage catalog with IDs, skills, procedures, complexity levels; references list; skills list
data_sources.ORCHESTRATOR.md: Orchestrator behavior, dual-mode architecture, dynamic graph details, compliance gates
data_sources.AGENTS.md: Directory structure, dual-mode explanation, framework vs project file separation

constraints: Keep it concise - this is a summary, not comprehensive documentation
Use tables for stages and architecture comparison
Use tree diagram for directory structure
Use numbered list for core principles
Do not include implementation details or code snippets beyond module names
